BC-ERR-01001: BC-QA-01003: When the function values at the point are also supplied and differ from the limits, combining the function values instead of the limits is the most common wrong answer, the archetype's own distractor list names it.
BC-ERR-01002: BC-QA-01002: When the tabulated outputs approach different values from the left and from the right, reporting the value one side approaches as the two sided limit is the characteristic wrong estimate on this archetype.

BC-QA-01013: Translating a one sided limit statement into a description of two sided behaviour (or a one ended statement at infinity into behaviour at both ends) is the one sided against two sided mismatch this archetype tests.
BC-ERR-01003: BC-QA-01002: Tables on this archetype are built for functions undefined at the target, and concluding that the limit does not exist because the function has no value there is a common wrong reading of such a table.

BC-QA-01014: When substitution gives a nonzero number over zero, declaring that the limit does not exist because the expression is undefined at the point, with no sign analysis on each side, is the procedure this error produces on the infinite limit draws.
BC-ERR-01008: BC-QA-04009: Before the rule is applied, a response that sees the numerator tend to zero and reports the limit as zero, ignoring the denominator, makes the record's indeterminate form read as the answer zero; it is a distinct wrong value on this archetype.
BC-ERR-01015: BC-QA-01007: At a removable break the one sided limits agree, and declaring the function continuous there from that agreement alone, ignoring that the function is undefined, is a classification error this archetype provokes.
BC-ERR-01019: BC-QA-01014: On a nonzero over zero draw with a simple factor in the denominator, the procedure of writing one two sided infinite limit, skipping the sign check on each side, is exactly this error.
BC-ERR-01020: BC-QA-01007: At an infinite break, writing that the limit equals infinity and then treating that as an existing limit leads to classifying the break as removable.
BC-QA-01013: Reading a statement that a one sided limit is infinite as saying that the limit exists as a real number is a common mistranslation of an infinite limit statement.

BC-QA-01014: On a nonzero over zero draw with a squared factor in the denominator, concluding that the limit exists because it equals infinity is exactly this error and a common wrong end to the procedure.
BC-ERR-01021: BC-QA-01013: Reading a limit at infinity as the value of the function at an input called infinity treats infinity as a number, which is a common mistranslation of an end behaviour statement.
BC-QA-01014: On a limit at infinity draw, substituting infinity into the quotient and simplifying infinity over infinity as 1 is the wrong procedure this error names.
BC-ERR-01023: BC-QA-01014: On a limit at infinity draw where the numerator has lower degree, taking the ratio of the leading coefficients without comparing degrees is the wrong procedure this error names.
BC-ERR-02016: BC-QA-02007: Sums of sine, cosine, exponential and logarithm terms usually carry a constant term, and students keep that constant in the derivative exactly as they do in polynomial sums.
BC-ERR-02021: BC-QA-02010: The archetype's path rewrites the function over sine or cosine and applies the quotient rule, where reversing the numerator terms flips the sign of the derivative of tangent or secant.
BC-ERR-02024: BC-QA-02013: Asked for the derivative at an input with a calculator, students report the function value there, which is a function value used where a derivative value was required.

BC-QA-02003: After identifying the underlying function and base point, reporting the function's value there instead of its derivative's value is a common wrong answer on this archetype, named in its own distractor list.
BC-ERR-02026: BC-QA-02008: The archetype's quotients have a sine or cosine in the numerator or the denominator, and differentiating that quotient as the numerator's derivative over the denominator's derivative is exactly the term-by-term error this record describes.
BC-ERR-03001: BC-QA-03003: Reading the composite derivative from graphs, students report the outer slope at the inner output and never multiply by the inner slope, the inner derivative omitted.
BC-ERR-03003: BC-QA-04009: When the numerator is f(kx) and f' is given at several inputs, differentiating f(kx) and reading f' at x = a instead of at ka is the record's outer derivative read at the input rather than at the inner output.
BC-ERR-03004: BC-QA-03003: The two slopes read from the graphs are added instead of multiplied, the same combination by addition recorded for table values.
BC-ERR-03012: BC-QA-05012: Asked for the points of an implicit relation where the tangent is horizontal, a response that sets the denominator of dy/dx to zero reports the vertical tangent points instead; the archetype lists treating a vanishing denominator as a horizontal tangent as a common distractor, and the record describes exactly this exchange of the two conditions.
BC-ERR-03022: BC-QA-02012: When the supplied notation is a second derivative, converting between f double prime and the Leibniz form produces the malformed forms this error records, such as the square of dy/dx.
BC-ERR-04017: BC-QA-02012: Converting dV/dt into words or prime notation, students swap the roles of the two variables and read it as the rate of t with respect to V, which is differentiation with respect to the wrong variable.
BC-ERR-04023: BC-QA-02011: Writing the tangent line, students put the derivative value where the function value belongs and the function value where the slope belongs, the point and the slope exchanged.
BC-ERR-05013: BC-QA-07010: The archetype's common distractors include classifying with no sign statement; declaring an extremum wherever the right side vanishes, whether or not it changes sign, is this record's error.
BC-ERR-05021: BC-QA-07010: Classifying the critical point of a solution from the sign of the right side on each side can be done with the direction of the sign change reversed, reporting a maximum where the derivative goes from negative to positive.
BC-ERR-05025: BC-QA-07010: The archetype's common distractors include ignoring the supplied bound that removes a factor, which leaves a zero of the right side outside the stated range among the candidates.
BC-ERR-05028: BC-QA-09011: Finding the point farthest from an axis ends in a candidates comparison of the coordinate at the critical angle and the endpoints, and students who build that comparison correctly still report the candidate nearest the axis, the same wrong-direction selection the record describes, often after comparing negative coordinate values by sign instead of by distance.
BC-ERR-05057: BC-QA-03005: On an implicit curve with a singular point, setting the numerator of dy/dx to zero also returns the point where the denominator vanishes, and students report it as a horizontal tangent without checking the denominator, which is this record's error on a relation instead of an explicit function.
BC-ERR-05060: BC-QA-03008: Differentiating a dy/dx expression that contains y to get the second derivative, students treat y as a constant and drop every dy/dx term, which is this record's error outside the unit 5 setting it was first recorded in.
BC-ERR-06018: BC-QA-06011: The archetype's difficulty variables include an integrand that needs a substitution first, and its common distractors include keeping the original limits after a substitution; the record already lists BC-QA-06011 among its archetypes.
